CCaccc_acting_challenge_1558_cc accc_acting_challengewith_dialogue · no_ref · 127 takes
SAY: I thought I'd feel... more. More tears, more ache. Just dust motes in the sun. God, the quiet isn't heavy. It's just... air. I can walk loud now. No one to hear.
original DramaBox prompt & direction text

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A 38-year-old woman with a warm but weary timbre, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is struggling to hold onto a practiced sadness, but the familiar silence is making her unexpectedly restless. (letting out a slow breath) "I thought I'd feel... more. More tears, more ache." (pausing, listening to the creak) "Just dust motes in the sun." CUT TO: The same voice now lets out a surprised, private laugh as the emptiness finally feels like permission. (shaking her head, almost amused) "God, the quiet isn't heavy. It's just... air." (hearing her own footsteps) "I can walk loud now. No one to hear." The performance across both moments should feel like a single person slowly untangling grief from relief, each breath a small discovery.

CCaccc_acting_challenge_7796_cc accc_acting_challengewith_dialogue · no_ref · 128 takes
SAY: I was seven. I sat by the window every day after school. I thought you'd just been delayed. If I forgive you… does that mean what you did was okay? Was I that difficult to love?
original DramaBox prompt & direction text

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A 34-year-old woman with a voice that is clear and measured, carrying a faint tremor of old hurt, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is tightly controlled, as if she has rehearsed these words for years, but the stillness is brittle. (quiet, deliberate) "I was seven. I sat by the window every day after school." (a slow, measured exhale) "I thought you'd just been delayed." CUT TO: The same voice now cracks open into raw, childlike devastation, the adult composure gone. (voice breaking, barely a whisper) "If I forgive you… does that mean what you did was okay?" (a long, shuddering pause) "Was I that difficult to love?" The performance across both moments should feel like a dam breaking—from a rigid facade of composure to the naked, unfiltered ache of a child who never stopped waiting.

Direction only (dialogue removed — this is what prompt-sim compares against):

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A 27-year-old female with a hushed, slightly breathy timbre, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is frozen in confusion and embarrassment, speaking with agonizing restraint as she tries to justify a mistake. (voice barely above a whisper) "I just... I thought the chart was for room three." (swallows hard) "But the numbers didn't line up." (glances at the floor) "I'm sorry, I should have double-checked." (trails off) "I don't know what I was thinking." CUT TO: The same voice now sharp with indignation and sudden clarity, speaking with cold, restrained fury. (stares directly ahead) "No, that's not acceptable. I need the real numbers now." (firmly) "You will explain this to me right now." (flat but intense) "I've had enough of the confusion." The performance across both moments should feel like the same person transforming from paralyzed self-doubt to assertive clarity.

original DramaBox prompt & direction text

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A very old man with a brisk, forward-pushing tempo, a low, resonant but tremulous and breathy voice, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is impatient and irritable but threaded with hope and affection, as if waiting for something anticipated. "I swear, if that package doesn't show up today, I'll—but no, it's coming. They promised. And my granddaughter painted me a card, you know? She's seven. She uses too much glitter." (pause) "I'll keep it forever." CUT TO: The same voice now hollowed by grief, the hope drained away, speaking with a fragile, stunned quiet. "It's just... the card. That's all I have now. The glitter's still on my fingers. She was supposed to be here. She was supposed to—" (weakly) "—be here." The performance across both moments should feel like a single natural breath, from bustling expectancy to devastation, with the same old-man tremor and storybook cadence carrying through both.

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A 62-year-old man with a gravelly, weathered baritone, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is hunched forward, fists up, spit flying as he shoves past a trash can toward a younger attacker, contempt raw and animal in his throat. (spitting between words) "¡Métete con alguien de tu tamaño, pedazo de mierda!" (swinging, breath hissing) "Te voy a partir la madre, escúchame bien." (coughing, grabbing his side) "Te... te lo juro." (voice dropping, venom trembling) "Si le tocas un pelo más... te mato." The performance across both moments should feel like a single brutal breath—venomous fury collapsing into a wounded, whispered threat, every grunt and pause earned by real damage.

Full DramaBox prompt (how to say — with the "quoted" dialogue):
A child with a breathy, strained voice, delivering this high-quality studio voice recording with no background noise. The same voice is flushed and dizzy from being bent over, focused entirely on a stubborn knot in their shoelace. (breathing hard, words squeezed out) "No te muevas, tonto." (fingers fumbling) "Casi, casi está saliendo." CUT TO: The same voice now hot with frustration, a whine creeping in as the knot tightens and their arms start to shake. (a sharp exhale) "¡Ay, ya! ¿Por qué no te desatas?" (voice cracking with complaint) "Me duele la cabeza y esto no se mueve nada." The performance across both moments should feel like a real child's spiraling mood, from concentrated muttering to helpless whining, all while physically stuck in an uncomfortable pose.
